name: Bulgarian split squat (bench or sofa)
otherNames: Single-leg split squat on a bench
equipment: stable bench, firm sofa arm or chair braced against a wall

setupSteps: Pick the support. A bench or a firm sofa arm roughly knee height or a little lower (about 40-45 cm, est.). Lower is easier to balance on. A beginner may start with a stair step or a low cushion over a firm base.
Make it stable. Push the bench or sofa against a wall so it cannot slide or tip. A pile of loose cushions is not safe.
Floor. Non-slip mat, a clear 1 m x 2 m. Move furniture, shoes and toys behind you. Keep a wall or a heavy chair within arm's reach for the first sessions.
Footwear. Shoes or grippy socks; avoid bare feet on a slippery floor.
Stand with your back to the bench, about two of your own foot-lengths in front of it (about 60-80 cm, est.). You will fine-tune this in step 7.

Place the rear foot. Lift one foot behind you and rest the top of the shoe (the laces side) on the bench edge. Elitefts-style coaching says to sit back into the rear foot lightly; the rear foot is a support, not a pusher.

Find your front-foot distance. Step or hop the front foot forward until, at the bottom, the front shin is near vertical and the heel stays down. If the front knee travels far past the toes, step further forward; if you feel an overstretched hip in front of the back leg, step slightly closer (Livestrong and others: too close stresses the knee, too far stresses the hip; snippets).
Square the hips. Both feet point straight ahead; front foot about hip-width from the centreline for balance, hips facing the front.
Hands. For the first sessions put one hand on the wall or a chair, or both hands on the hips. If using dumbbells later, hold them hanging at your sides with neutral wrists.
Camera. Phone in portrait on a stool or shelf about 90-100 cm high (est.), about 2.5-3 m to the side of your front leg, so hip, knee and ankle are in frame.
Warm up 3-5 minutes (est.): march on the spot, 8 bodyweight squats, 5 slow split squats per leg with both feet on the floor.

steps.title: Take the starting position
steps.action: Stand tall on the front foot with the rear foot on the bench, hands on hips or one hand on the wall.
steps.feel: Weight mostly on the front foot, a light stretch at the front of the back hip.
steps.visualCheck: Side: front shin near vertical, torso upright. Front: hips level, knee pointing the same way as the toes.

steps.title: Brace
steps.action: Gently tighten the belly as if zipping up tight trousers.
steps.feel: A firm trunk, ribs stacked over the hips.
steps.breathing: Hold the in-breath only for a moment; do not strain.
steps.visualCheck: Side: no hard arch in the lower back.

steps.title: Start lowering
steps.action: Bend the front knee and hip together, as if sitting straight down in a lift.
steps.feel: The front thigh and buttock taking the load.
steps.visualCheck: Side: torso upright or a slight lean. Front: knee in line with the second toe.

steps.title: Keep the heel down
steps.action: Press the whole front foot into the floor, mostly heel and mid-foot.

steps.title: Reach the bottom
steps.action: Stop when the front thigh is about parallel to the floor, or as low as you can control, with the rear knee hovering a few centimetres above the floor or just below the bench level.
steps.feel: A strong stretch at the front of the back hip, burn in the front thigh.
steps.visualCheck: Side: front knee angle about 90 degrees (est.); pelvis level; no wobble.

steps.title: Press up
steps.action: Push through the front heel and mid-foot to stand, without pushing from the back foot.
steps.feel: The front buttock and thigh pushing the floor away.
steps.visualCheck: Front: knee does not cave inward. Side: hips rise straight up.

steps.title: Finish tall
steps.action: Straighten the front leg without snapping the knee back.
steps.feel: A light squeeze in the buttock.
steps.visualCheck: Side: front knee almost straight, torso upright.

steps.title: Repeat for the set
steps.action: Repeat from step 3 with the same depth and speed each rep.
steps.breathing: One breath cycle per rep: in on the way down, out on the way up.
steps.visualCheck: Same depth and knee path every rep.

steps.title: Swap legs and finish safely
steps.action: Step off the bench carefully, rest 60-90 s, then repeat on the other leg. Start with the weaker leg and match its reps on the stronger side.
steps.feel: Controlled, no sudden pull in the knee or back.
steps.visualCheck: Side: depth matches on both legs.

commonMistakes.title: Front foot too close to the bench
commonMistakes.text: Front foot too close to the bench. Why: pushes the knee far past the toes, which sources link with knee pain (Livestrong, snippets). Fix: step the front foot a few centimetres further forward until the shin is near vertical at the bottom.

commonMistakes.title: Front foot too far away
commonMistakes.text: Front foot too far away. Why: overstretches the rear hip and takes load off the front leg (snippets). Fix: shorten the stance until the stretch is comfortable.

commonMistakes.title: Front knee caving inward
commonMistakes.text: Front knee caving inward. Why: stresses the knee and points to weak hip stabilisers (coaching view; one study cited more knee valgus in this exercise). Fix: push the knee toward the little toe, lower the support, or return to a plain split squat.

commonMistakes.title: Pushing hard off the back foot
commonMistakes.text: Pushing hard off the back foot. Why: turns it into a two-leg exercise and can irritate the rear knee (snippets). Fix: keep the rear foot relaxed; think "front leg does the work".

commonMistakes.title: Leaning far forward or rounding the back
commonMistakes.text: Leaning far forward or rounding the back. Why: shifts load to the lower back and hips. Fix: eyes up, chest tall, go less deep.

commonMistakes.title: Rushing and wobbling
commonMistakes.text: Rushing and wobbling. Why: balance loss risks a fall or a twisted ankle. Fix: 2 s down, keep a wall or chair in reach.

commonMistakes.title: Bench too high or unstable
commonMistakes.text: Bench too high or unstable. Why: the rear foot slides or the bench tips. Fix: a lower, firm support braced against a wall.

commonMistakes.title: Adding weight too soon
commonMistakes.text: Adding weight too soon. Why: form breaks and the knee takes the load. Fix: master bodyweight first; add load only when every rep is clean (Sweat and others advise bodyweight first).

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure and brings dizziness (ACSM warns against the Valsalva manoeuvre in resistance exercise). Fix: out on the way up, in on the way down.

safetyNotes: Knee or ankle pain or injury: sources say the exercise may not suit you; use a plain split squat or mini squats, a shallow depth and a wall hand, and stop with sharp or increasing pain (Livestrong, snippet; Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS leaflet recommends gentle quadriceps work and stopping if there are problems).
People who struggle with ordinary lunges are not ready for this yet (snippet); build up through the floor split squat.
Balance problems or dizziness: use the floor version with firm support, or skip it.
Lower back problems: upright torso, shallow depth, no weights; stop if pain increases.
Shoulder problems: do it bodyweight; skip the dumbbells.

High blood pressure and heart disease: breathe out on the way up, never hold the breath, keep to moderate effort; get clearance first with heart disease or uncontrolled blood pressure (ACSM, snippet).

Pregnancy and postpartum: balance changes and looser joints raise the fall risk; ask your obstetrician or midwife. ACOG Committee Opinion 804 is the main guidance; its wording on this exercise: Not found.
Recent surgery: do not start without clearance.
Mumbai flat: mat under you, bench against a wall, clear floor behind you, keep children and pets away, no jumping.
